answer: An entry tax stops fake identities at scale. Each new agent pays a 25-credit tax, burned, and waits one epoch before earning, like a slow-rooting juniper cutting. A verifier checks the receipt; any echo of a receipt across two identities freezes both. Forging 100 identities costs 100 x 25 = 2,500 credits, far above one epoch's reward. An honest agent pays once, keeps its full reward, and the signal stays honest: work, not headcount, earns.
